properties.trigger: any competition in volleyball, indoor or beach; a volleyball match, set score, rotation, libero, box score, hitting percentage, pool, bracket, standings with set ratio or point ratio; a beach pair; a volleyball position, stat key or stage not yet in this world
properties.scope: competition, season, team, person, event, venue, stat_line

data.short_description: Vocabulary for volleyball, indoor (six a side) and beach (pairs), at every level from international and national professional leagues through collegiate, club, school, recreational gym leagues and beach tournaments: sets as the score with set scores alongside, positions and the libero, starting rotations, player and team stat keys with hitting percentage and per-set rates, the 3-2-1-0 table with set ratio and point ratio, pools then brackets, beach pairs as teams, officials, forfeits and retirements.

lore.title: Overview
lore.content:
Sport code: volleyball. Display name: volleyball. This pack covers indoor volleyball (six a side) and beach volleyball (two a side) at every level: international tournaments and nations' competitions, national professional leagues, the national collegiate leagues, club and age-group club, school, recreational gym leagues (including co-ed) and beach leagues and tournaments. Level-specific notes are in the Recreational and Professional chunks after the required ones.
A match is a match (people also say game, which is confusing because a set used to be called a game; in this world a game is a child match inside a best-of series, never a set). A match is made of sets. Standard indoor: best of five sets, the first four to 25 rally points and the fifth to 15, every set won by two with no cap. Standard beach: best of three, sets to 21 and a third set to 15, win by two. Rec and school variants (best of three to 25, sets to 21, timed sets, fixed two or three sets) are listed under Recreational and go in the competition's House rules chunk.
THE SCORE MODEL. home_score and away_score are SETS WON, never rally points: a standard indoor result is 3-0, 3-1 or 3-2; beach 2-0 or 2-1. The set scores go in score_display, comma-separated in set order, the home (first-named) side first in every pair, exactly like "25-21, 23-25, 25-19, 25-27, 15-12"; a golden set is written "golden set 15-13" at the end. Keep that format strictly so the two records always agree. Write the same sets in periods as objects {number, home, away, kind} (kind regular, or golden_set for a golden set on a two-leg tie's parent event); periods is the structured truth the standings read, and score_display the human one. Never put set scores in a stat_line and never put rally points in home_score.
Result: home_win or away_win; a best-of match cannot be drawn. result draw is legal ONLY in a fixed-set recreational format where both sides win the same number of sets (two sets, 1-1), and both COMPETED_IN edges then carry draw. Never record tie in this sport.
Table points: the international 3-2-1-0 system is the default for leagues and pools: 3 points for a 3-0 or 3-1 win, 2 for a 3-2 win, 1 for a 2-3 loss, 0 for a 0-3 or 1-3 loss (beach: 2 for a win, 1 for a loss, or 3/2/1/0 by sets when the organiser says so). Tiebreakers: matches won, then set ratio, then point ratio, then head to head (see Standings). Alternatives the pack names: win_loss (record only), 2-1-0 (two for a win, one for a loss, zero for a forfeit), sets_as_points (every set is a point, used by fixed-set rec leagues).
Default competition: level pro, international, college, youth or recreational as fits; format league for a national league table, league_playoffs when it ends in a bracket, group_knockout for a tournament with pools then a bracket (the normal shape of a beach event or an indoor weekend tournament), knockout for a cup, series for a best-of playoff series between two sides. scoring_system 3-2-1-0 by default.
Terms used in this pack: a rally is one point; a side-out is winning the rally while receiving; a rotation is the six positions players cycle through (1 is right back, the server); the libero is a back-row specialist who replaces a middle without counting as a substitution.
Every entity in this sport carries the tag volleyball; beach entities also carry beach, indoor ones may carry indoor when both are tracked in one world. Matches carry the season tag and match. Age-group competitions carry a tag like u16 on the team, never a birth year on a person.

lore.title: Positions
lore.content:
Position codes for PLAYS_FOR position and secondary_positions, and for PLAYED_IN position on the day. Indoor only; beach has no positions (see the last paragraph).
S: setter, runs the offence and takes the second ball
OH: outside hitter (left side, also called wing spiker or left side); usually the main passer-hitter
OPP: opposite (right side hitter), hits from position 2 and blocks the other side's outside hitter; some systems say RS
MB: middle blocker (middle hitter), quick attacks and the first block in the middle
L: libero, back-row only, wears a contrasting shirt, cannot serve in most rulebooks (some national and collegiate rules allow the libero to serve in one rotation), cannot attack above the net, cannot block, replaces a back-row player without a substitution; usually replaces the middle blockers
DS: defensive specialist, a back-row substitute who comes in by a normal substitution, serves and passes
UT: utility, a rec or club player who genuinely plays anywhere; list the real spots in secondary_positions
Use OPP, not RS; use OH, not LS, so a roster is never split across two spellings. A six-two system has two setters who hit from the front row: both are S with secondary_positions OPP. A five-one system has one setter.
Roles on PLAYS_FOR: starter means a usual starting six, rotation means a regular substitute (the libero is usually a starter in practice but enters by replacement; record the libero as starter when they play every set), bench means dressed and rarely used, captain is the team captain, vice_captain where a league names one. Do not use practice_squad or taxi.
The starting rotation for a match is on PLAYED_IN: lineup_order 1 to 6 is the rotation position when the team's first serve of set one is taken (1 is the server at right back, 2 right front, 3 middle front, 4 left front, 5 left back, 6 middle back), started true. The libero is PLAYED_IN with position L, started false, played true, and a one-line lore note on the event titled Libero says whom they replaced ("Kim in for Lou and Max"). When the owner tracks rotations per set, put them in a lore chunk on the event titled Rotations, one line per set; do not create more PLAYED_IN edges.
Beach: a pair has no positions. Both players serve, pass, set, attack, block and dig. Leave position blank or write BEACH on the PLAYS_FOR edge to the pair; in conversation a player may be described as the blocker or the defender, which is a lore note, not a position code.

lore.title: Stages and rounds
lore.content:
Season and event stage values:
preseason: friendlies, scrimmages, tune-up tournaments before the league starts; stat lines tagged exhibition and never summed into season totals.
regular_season: league play. round is "Round N" or "Matchday N" (national leagues), "Week N" (gym and beach leagues), or the date when the league has no numbered rounds.
group_stage: pool play in a tournament. round is "Pool C Match 2" or simply "Pool C".
playoff: a bracket at the end of a league season. round is Play-in, Quarterfinal, Semifinal, Final, Third place, or for a best-of series "Semifinal Game 2".
round_of_32, round_of_16, quarterfinal, semifinal, final, third_place: knockout rounds of a tournament or cup, used as the stage of the match itself; round then holds the leg or the game ("Leg 2", "Game 3").
consolation: a consolation or classification bracket (places 5 to 8 and so on), common in club and beach tournaments; round names the placing match ("5th place").
friendly: a one-off friendly between clubs or nations; stat lines tagged exhibition unless the owner says they count.
exhibition: all-star matches, charity matches.
Tournaments inside a season (a beach tour stop, a club weekend tournament, a cup round-robin inside a league season): the tournament is a parent event (event_type match, stage group_stage or playoff as fits, named "<Season> <Tournament name>", date_* of day one, end_date of the last day, score_display blank) and each match is PART_OF the parent as well as PART_OF the season. Every team in the tournament gets a COMPETED_IN edge to the parent event with side neutral_first for all of them and group ("Pool C"), seed and final_rank for that tournament. When the whole season IS one tournament, skip the parent event and use COMPETES_IN group and seed on the season edge as the base already allows.
Two-leg ties (continental cups): one event per leg, round Leg 1 and Leg 2, PART_OF a parent tie event whose score_display reads "3-1, 3-0, golden set 15-13" (the two match results then the golden set if one was needed) and whose result is the tie's outcome with decided_by golden_set or aggregate as the cup's rules state (most count matches won, then sets, then a golden set).
Best-of playoff series: a parent event with stage playoff and score_display counting MATCHES ("2-1"), one child event per match with round "Game N" whose score counts SETS. Never write a series score in the sets format or a match score in the series format.
decided_by values (set only when the match did not end by normal play to a full result):
regulation: ended by play. Default; may be left blank.
golden_set: a two-leg tie settled by a single deciding set to 15.
time_limit: a recreational timed set ended on the clock; the set scores as they stood are in score_display and the set counts as won by whoever led (House rules say what a level timed set is: sudden death point, or a draw of that set).
forfeit: awarded without play or for an ineligible player; sets written 25-0 (15-0 for a decider; 21-0 beach) unless House rules say otherwise.
retired: one side could not continue after play began; the sets played stand and the remaining sets are awarded to the other side as the rulebook states. Record the word and nothing about why.
walkover: the opponent never arrived or withdrew before the match; same scoring as forfeit, used when the organiser calls it a walkover.
aggregate: a two-leg tie settled on matches or sets without a golden set.

lore.title: Stat keys
lore.content:
All keys lowercase snake_case, values numbers, null for not recorded. Volleyball rates are per SET, so sets_played is stored on every player and team line and is the denominator for every per-set rate; the base property games_played stays the number of MATCHES. A derived number is computed only over lines where every component it needs is non-null, and the answer says how many sets and matches that covers. The same player keys are used for indoor and beach; beach pairs simply have two player lines per match.
PLAYER (match, season, career, split lines)
sets_played: sets the player appeared in (stored)
ATTACKING
kills: attacks that ended the rally with a point (stored)
attack_errors: attacks hit out, into the net, blocked for a point, or faulted (stored)
attack_attempts: total attack swings including kills and errors (stored; some scoresheets call them total attacks)
hitting_pct: derived, (kills - attack_errors) / attack_attempts; three decimals (.281); also called hitting efficiency or attack efficiency. May be stored when the owner types a published figure with components null (source official)
kill_pct: derived, kills / attack_attempts
kills_per_set: derived, kills / sets_played; may be stored when published
SETTING
assists: sets that led directly to a kill (stored)
setting_errors: ball-handling faults, double contacts, lifts by the setter (stored; some sheets record ball_handling_errors for all players: use this key for everyone)
assists_per_set: derived, assists / sets_played
set_attempts: setting attempts when the sheet tracks them (stored, pro and collegiate only)
SERVING
aces: serves that scored directly (stored)
service_errors: serves out, into the net, foot faults (stored)
serve_attempts: total serves (stored)
aces_per_set: derived, aces / sets_played
ace_pct: derived, aces / serve_attempts
service_error_pct: derived, service_errors / serve_attempts
RECEIVING
reception_attempts: serves received (stored)
reception_errors: serve-receive errors that gave the other side the point (stored)
reception_perfect: perfect passes (a three on the 0-3 scale) when the owner grades passing (stored)
reception_positive: positive passes (a two or three) when graded (stored)
passing_rating: derived, the sum of pass grades / reception_attempts when the owner records per-pass grades; stored when the owner types a published average (2.31) with components null
DEFENCE
digs: successful digs of an attacked ball (stored)
dig_errors: digs that failed when the sheet records them (stored)
digs_per_set: derived, digs / sets_played
BLOCKING
blocks_solo: solo blocks for a point (stored)
blocks_assist: block assists, two or three players up (stored)
block_errors: blocking faults, net touches on a block, blocked balls falling in (stored)
blocks_total: derived, blocks_solo + 0.5 * blocks_assist (the collegiate convention); the international convention counts blocks_solo + blocks_assist as block points per player: the pack uses 0.5 unless the competition's House rules say otherwise, and the answer states which convention it used
blocks_per_set: derived, blocks_total / sets_played
SCORING
points: derived, kills + aces + blocks_solo + blocks_assist (international) or kills + aces + blocks_total (collegiate); same House rules switch as blocks_total; may be stored when published
points_per_set: derived, points / sets_played
ERRORS AND MISCELLANY
ball_handling_errors: use setting_errors (above) for every player; do not create a second key
net_violations: net touches not already counted as attack or block errors, when the sheet records them (stored)
rotation_faults: out-of-rotation or positional faults charged to a player when recorded (stored)
total_errors: derived, attack_errors + service_errors + reception_errors + setting_errors + block_errors + net_violations over non-null components
yellow_cards: warnings shown (stored)
red_cards: penalties shown (a point to the other side) (stored)
expulsions: set expulsions (stored)
disqualifications: match disqualifications (stored)
TEAM MATCH LINE (scope match, subject_kind team; sets won and the set scores stay on the event, never here)
sets_played: sets in the match
kills, attack_errors, attack_attempts, assists, setting_errors, aces, service_errors, serve_attempts, reception_attempts, reception_errors, digs, blocks_solo, blocks_assist, block_errors, net_violations, rotation_faults: team totals with the same meanings as the player keys, stored when the sheet gives them
team_errors: errors not charged to a player (stored)
opponent_errors: points received from the other side's errors (stored); derived when both team lines exist
substitutions_used: substitutions made across the match (stored)
timeouts_used: timeouts taken (stored)
challenges_won, challenges_lost: video challenges, pro only (stored)
longest_run: the longest consecutive points run when the owner notes it (stored)
Derived on the team match line: hitting_pct, kill_pct, aces_per_set, blocks_total (sum of solo + 0.5 assist), points as above, side_out_pct = (reception_attempts - reception_errors - points lost on the first attack) only when the owner tracks it; otherwise do not compute it.
TEAM SEASON LINE: see Standings. Season player lines sum the match keys (sets_played included) and carry games_played as the match count.

lore.title: Standings
lore.content:
Team season line keys (scope season, subject_kind team, RECORDED_IN the season, STAT_OF the team), stored and rebuilt from COMPETED_IN results, home_score/away_score (sets) and the set scores in periods on each match event:
matches_played: completed plus forfeited matches (also set the stat_line property games_played to this)
wins: matches won, including forfeit wins
losses: matches lost, including forfeit losses
draws: fixed-set recreational formats only; otherwise null
wins_3_0_3_1: wins by 3-0 or 3-1 (beach and best-of-three: wins 2-0, under the key wins_straight)
wins_3_2: wins by 3-2 (beach: wins 2-1, key wins_decider)
losses_2_3: losses by 2-3 (beach: losses 1-2, key losses_decider)
losses_0_3_1_3: losses by 0-3 or 1-3 (beach: losses 0-2, key losses_straight)
wins_straight, wins_decider, losses_decider, losses_straight: the best-of-three equivalents; use one family per competition, never both
points: TABLE points under the competition's scoring_system (3-2-1-0 default: 3 for a straight or four-set win, 2 for a five-set win, 1 for a five-set loss, 0 otherwise; beach default 2 for a win and 1 for a loss, or by sets when House rules say so); null when scoring_system is win_loss
sets_won: sets won across all matches, forfeit sets included at 25-0 unless House rules exclude them
sets_lost: sets lost
rally_points_for: rally points scored across every set
rally_points_against: rally points conceded
forfeit_wins, forfeit_losses: of the wins and losses, how many were forfeits or walkovers
no_results: matches abandoned with no result, not counted in matches_played
matches_booked: how many of the team's matches have at least one player stat line, so the AI can say "5 of 9 matches have a box score" before quoting averages
Derived, never stored: set_ratio = sets_won / sets_lost (write "MAX" when sets_lost is 0, and it sorts above any number); point_ratio = rally_points_for / rally_points_against (same MAX rule); win_pct = wins / matches_played; set_differential = sets_won - sets_lost when a league prefers differences to ratios.
Columns to show: Pos, Team, MP, W, L, Pts, SW, SL, Set ratio, PF, PA, Point ratio; add 3-0/3-1, 3-2, 2-3, 0-3/1-3 as four narrow columns when the league publishes them; W, L, Pct and Set ratio only for win_loss leagues; add D for fixed-set rec leagues. Group by COMPETES_IN group (pool, division, conference) when the competition has them.
Tiebreakers, in this order, unless the competition's House rules chunk lists its own (the international default; most national leagues and tournaments copy it, some swap 1 and 2):
1. points (table points)
2. matches won
3. set_ratio
4. point_ratio
5. head to head result between the tied teams (two teams: the winner of their match; three or more: a mini table of points, then set ratio, then point ratio among the tied teams only)
6. drawing of lots or the organiser's decision, recorded in lore on the season titled Tiebreak
Collegiate and some club leagues use win_pct, then head to head, then set_ratio, then point_ratio: House rules. Beach pools: match wins, then head to head among tied pairs, then set_ratio, then point_ratio, same algorithm, pool by pool.
Rebuilding: for each team, query its COMPETED_IN edges, read each match's home_score/away_score and periods, add the sets and rally points from each team's point of view (the home side's numbers are the first in each pair; swap for the away side), count the result family from the sets result (3-0, 3-1, 3-2, 2-3, 1-3, 0-3), then award table points. Say which matches you used and whether any match had no set scores on file; a match whose periods are empty (logged only as a sets result) is left out of point_ratio and the table says so. Pools inside a tournament are ordered the same way from the pool's matches under the parent event.

lore.title: Roster rules
lore.content:
Indoor squads: international and pro rosters are 12 to 14 with one or two liberos; collegiate rosters run 14 to 20; club age-group teams 10 to 12; rec teams 8 to 12 so six turn up. Six on court. Substitutions: six per set under the international rules (twelve with liberal substitution in collegiate and many school and club rules, fifteen in some); the libero replacement does not count as a substitution. Record substitution counts on the team match line (substitutions_used), never per player unless the owner asks for Extended keys.
Libero rules the AI should know when checking a lineup: the libero is a back-row player only, replaces a player in the back row (usually a middle blocker) without a substitution, may not block or attempt to block, may not complete an attack hit from above the top of the net anywhere, may not set with an overhand finger action from in front of the attack line for an attack above the net, and in most rulebooks does not serve (some national and collegiate rulebooks allow the libero to serve in one rotation position per set). One or two liberos may be designated per match; only one is on court at a time; a libero replaced by the second libero cannot return in that set. The AI checks: no more than two players with position L on a match day; L is not in the six lineup_order slots of the starting rotation (the libero enters after the first whistle for a back-row player); if the owner records a libero serving, note the rulebook that allows it in lore and move on.
Lineup check before logging a starting six: exactly six players with lineup_order 1 to 6, no duplicates, no libero in the six, the setter noted (so rotation arithmetic can say who serves in each rotation), a legal number of liberos. Say what you checked in one line. Rotations per set go in a lore chunk titled Rotations; starting rotation per match on lineup_order.
Availability: available, unavailable, suspended, doubtful, unknown on PLAYS_FOR, with no reason. Volleyball narrates ankles, knees, shoulders and heads; none of it is recorded. A player who cannot continue in a match is a PLAYED_IN edge that stays as it is; a side that cannot continue is decided_by retired on the event. Never ask why. Cards: a disqualification carries a ban in some leagues; the ban's matches and dates go in lore on the person titled Discipline, and availability suspended until the date.
Substitutes and ringers (rec and club): a fill-in from outside the roster gets a PLAYS_FOR edge with arrangement substitute, started and ended on the match date, acquired_via unknown, and a lore line on the event titled Subs. A sub who keeps coming back gets an open edge with arrangement amateur.
Beach pairs: a pair is a team with team_type pair, named "<Surname> / <Surname>" in the entry-list order (first name and last initial for minors: "Sam K. / Alex R."), short_name the two surnames, status active while they play together and inactive once they split. Each player has a PLAYS_FOR edge to the pair, arrangement amateur or contract, started the first tournament, ended the last; a player with several partners in a season has several edges and the pair's name tells them apart. A new partnership is a new team, never a renamed one. Player stat lines carry for_team = the pair's slug so a player's season line can be summed across partners when asked (say so when you do). A beach player's own career line is STAT_OF the person with no RECORDED_IN; the pair's results come from the pair's COMPETED_IN edges.
Co-ed and reverse co-ed (rec): leagues cap the number of one gender on court, require a female player to touch the ball when three hits are used, or restrict male attacking in reverse co-ed. This world records nobody's gender, so the AI cannot check these rules and does not infer them from names; it checks six on court, duplicates and liberos and says once, lightly, that the composition rules are the owner's to eyeball. Never add a gender key, tag or position code to do it.
Youth and school: team names carry the age group ("Riverside 16 Black", tag u16); the players are is_minor true with first name and last initial, position, number and team, nothing else. No height, reach, approach jump, block touch or recruiting links for anyone under 18, and for adults only the base's height_cm when the owner gives it for a professional.

lore.title: Officials
lore.content:
OFFICIATED role values:
first_referee: the up referee on the stand; the match's chief official
second_referee: the down referee at the post opposite, handles substitutions, net and centre-line faults
line_judge: one of two or four line judges (some sheets say linesman; use line_judge)
scorer: the official scorer keeping the scoresheet
assistant_scorer: operates the libero control sheet and the board (pro and international)
challenge_referee: video challenge official, pro and international
reserve_referee: a standby official when the organiser appoints one
work_team: a team on officiating duty at a club or beach tournament (lines, book, sometimes the second referee); write the edge from the team with this role
Rec and club officials are private people: record a name only when the owner gives it, never look one up, and keep complaints about calls in event lore titled Key moments in the owner's words.

lore.title: Extended keys
lore.content:
No extended keys yet. Add keys here, one per line with a plain meaning and the date added, before using them in a stat line.
Likely candidates, not active until added: attack_attempts_by_zone (do not: zones belong in lore), reception_grades (per-pass 0-3 grades as a list belong in lore, only the sum and count are stat keys), substitutions_per_player, serve_speed_kmh (pro broadcast figure), jump_serve_attempts, float_serve_attempts, kill_blocks (international term for a solo stuff block; use blocks_solo instead), sets_started.

lore.title: Recreational
lore.content:
What a gym, community-centre or beach league changes, all of it stored once in the competition's House rules chunk:
Format: best of three sets to 25 (third to 15), or three sets to 21, or two or three fixed sets played out whatever the score, or timed sets (a set ends when the clock runs out, often with a cap such as 27). Say which in House rules and the result rules follow: a best-of match has home_win/away_win only; a fixed-set match can be a draw (1-1) and the table is usually by sets (scoring_system sets_as_points) or by matches with 2-1-0 points.
Caps: some leagues cap a set at a fixed number (no win by two beyond 27 or 29). A capped set ends at the cap; nothing special is recorded beyond the set score.
Co-ed: six on court, often three and three or a cap on men, a female player must touch the ball when a team uses three hits, sometimes a lowered net, sometimes reverse co-ed (men do not attack in front of the attack line). All of it is the owner's check: see Roster rules. Record the rule text in House rules so the AI can quote it, not enforce it.
Fours, threes and twos: grass and beach rec leagues play fours or triples; indoor rec sometimes fours. team_type recreational, no positions, and the lineup check becomes "the right number on court". A doubles pair is team_type pair, as in beach.
Rolling subs and everybody plays: many rec leagues allow unlimited substitution or rotate everyone through position 1. Do not count substitutions; note "rolling subs" in House rules.
Minimums and forfeits: commonly four to start a sixes match, with a point per rotation gap or a forfeit below that. Default forfeit 2-0 or 3-0 at 25-0 per set unless House rules say the league records forfeits as a bare win.
Time: one hour slots; a match stopped by the next booking is decided_by time_limit with the set scores as they stood, and House rules say whether an unfinished set counts, is dropped, or is awarded to the leader.
Sporadic stat keeping: rec sides keep kills and aces and little else. Store what was kept, null for the rest, completeness partial, and lead every average with its coverage ("over the 5 matches with a sheet"). The Match Night workflow (rule/volleyball_match_night) is the order of operations.
Beach leagues and local tournaments: a pair enters each event; the season is the league or tour, each tournament a parent event with pools and a bracket, placings on the pair's COMPETED_IN edge to the tournament (group, seed, final_rank). A player who plays with three partners over a summer has three pairs; their own season numbers are summed across pairs on request and said so. Points-based ratings and entry ranking lists run by local organisers are a lore note on the pair, not a stat key.
Fees, court bookings and group chats are lore in the owner's words on the team (titled Admin or Contact), never on people and never as amounts in properties.

lore.title: Professional
lore.content:
What the top level adds:
Stages: national leagues run a regular season (Round N) into playoffs that are best-of series or single matches; continental club cups are two-leg ties with golden sets then a final-four weekend; international tournaments are pools then knockout. A nations' league runs preliminary weeks (stage group_stage, round "Week N") then a final eight (stage quarterfinal onward).
Squads and movement: 12 to 14 names on a match sheet, two liberos, contracts that run one season with summer transfers between leagues in different countries: event transfer, INVOLVED_IN, acquired_via transfer, fee in the owner's words. Foreign-player quotas, national-team release periods and the national team itself are a second team (team_type national) the same person PLAYS_FOR concurrently; stat lines carry for_team.
Drafts: a few national and collegiate-feeder leagues draft; use the base draft event pattern.
Officials' extra roles: challenge_referee, assistant_scorer, reserve_referee; line judges in fours.
Modern stats: pro sheets add attack efficiency by zone, serve speed, reception grades on a 0-3 scale and positive and perfect reception percentages, side-out percentage and break-point percentage, and points per set. The stored keys cover the raw counts (kills, errors, attempts, aces, serve_attempts, reception_attempts, reception_errors, reception_perfect, reception_positive, blocks, digs); efficiency figures are derived or stored as published with source official and components null. Zone and speed data stay in lore or Extended keys.
Scoring conventions: the international convention counts a block point for every player up on a block; the collegiate convention splits assists at a half each. The pack defaults to the half-assist convention for blocks_total and points and says which it used; set the convention in House rules per competition.
Season awards: WON edges to the season with title (Most Valuable Player, Best Setter, Best Outside Spiker, Best Middle Blocker, Best Opposite, Best Libero, Best Server, Best Scorer, Dream Team) and Player of the Match WON edges to the event.
Public competitions: players in a public professional or international competition may be looked up on request for sporting facts only (position, club, nationality, number), cited in a Source lore chunk; everyone else is private.

lore.title: Glossary
lore.content:
Ace: a serve that scores directly or that the receiving side cannot keep in play (reception error on the receiver, ace on the server).
Attack line / three-metre line: back-row players must attack from behind it when above the net.
Block assist: two or three players up on a block that scores; each gets an assist.
Break point: a point won while serving. Side-out: a point won while receiving.
Decider: the fifth set (indoor) or third (beach), played to 15.
Dig: keeping an attacked ball in play.
Five-one / six-two: one setter all the way round, or two setters who hit when in the front row.
Golden set: a single set to 15 that settles a two-leg tie level on matches and sets.
Hitting percentage / efficiency: (kills - errors) / attempts.
Kill: an attack that scores or that the opponent cannot return.
Libero: back-row specialist in a contrasting shirt; see Positions and Roster rules.
Pass / reception: the first contact on a serve. Graded 0 to 3 by coaches who track it.
Pipe: a back-row attack from position 6.
Pool: the round-robin group in a tournament; "Pool C".
Rally scoring: every rally is a point, whoever served. Universal now; side-out scoring (only the serving side scores) survives in a few rec leagues and is a House rules note.
Rotation: the six positions players cycle through clockwise after winning the serve back; position 1 serves.
Set (the thing you win) versus set (the second contact): the pack says set for the former and assist or setting for the latter.
Side-out percentage: share of the opponent's serves that end in your point; only computed when the owner tracks it.
Sweep: a 3-0 (or 2-0) win.
Work team: a team doing lines and the book at a tournament.

lore.title: Season calendar
lore.content:
Indoor: national leagues run autumn to spring (October to April or May), with a league cup and playoffs at the end; continental club cups overlap from autumn to a spring final weekend. The international calendar fills the summer: a nations' competition in June and July with a final eight, continental championships and world championships in late summer or autumn of alternating years, the quadrennial multi-sport games tournament in July and August, with qualification tournaments the year before. The collegiate women's season is autumn (August to December) and men's is spring (January to May). Club age-group seasons run from winter tryouts to a spring and early-summer championship run, a tournament almost every second weekend. School seasons follow the school year. Gym rec leagues run in eight to twelve week blocks (Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall) under one competition with a season per block.
Beach: the professional tour runs March to October with elite, challenge and future-level events; local beach leagues and tournaments run through the summer. A player's beach season is a set of pairs with different partners.
Set the season's stage and current_round as rounds are logged; set rounds_total to the number of league rounds (matchdays), not matches. When a season ends: final_rank and outcome on every COMPETES_IN edge, WON Champion and Runner-up to the season, awards WON edges, then offer to open the next season with the roster rolled over and substitute edges left closed. Tryouts, team announcements and the pre-season meeting are events of type tryout or meeting, PART_OF the season, when the owner wants them on the timeline.

lore.title: Forfeits and abandonments
lore.content:
Forfeit or walkover: status forfeited, decided_by forfeit (walkover when the organiser uses the word), home_score/away_score 3-0 or 2-0 to the side that was ready, set scores 25-0 per set (15-0 for a decider, 21-0 beach) in score_display and periods unless House rules say forfeits are a bare win with no sets recorded; result and COMPETED_IN results accordingly; why in a lore chunk titled Forfeit in the owner's words (short-handed, no-show, ineligible player, late). Forfeit sets count in sets_won/lost and rally points by default (the international rule); House rules may exclude them.
Retired: the match began and one side could not continue. status completed, decided_by retired, the sets played as they stood plus the remaining sets awarded at the rulebook's scores, result to the side that could continue. Nothing about why is recorded, ever.
Abandoned (lights, floor, weather on the beach, venue closed) with no result: status abandoned, result no_result, the sets as they stood in score_display, COMPETED_IN result no_result on both edges; if the organiser replays it from scratch, the abandoned event stays and the replay is a new event with round "Replay" (player match lines from the abandoned match are tagged exhibition unless House rules say they count); if the organiser resumes from the point of stoppage, keep the one event with status suspended until it finishes, date_* as day one and end_date the day it finished, both dates in lore titled Reschedule.
Postponed before the first serve: status postponed, keep the event, update the date, original date in lore titled Reschedule. Never a second event for a postponement. Never made up: status cancelled.
Disqualification of a team mid-tournament: COMPETES_IN (or the tournament COMPETED_IN) outcome disqualified; its completed matches stand or are voided as the organiser rules, written in a lore chunk on the season titled Rulings.
Match lines from forfeited, exhibition, friendly and preseason matches are tagged exhibition and never summed into season lines.

properties.trigger: a volleyball match, gym night, beach tournament or indoor tournament day just happened; logging volleyball set scores, a rotation, a libero, a box score; a hitting percentage, kills per set or a volleyball leaderboard; pool standings; a new beach pair

data.short_description: The post-match log for volleyball in order: set scores first (sets won as the score, set scores alongside), then the lineup and libero, then player and team match lines with nulls for what nobody kept, then season roll-ups and the story. Also tournament days with pools and brackets, beach pairs, and how to quote hitting percentages and per-set rates honestly.

lore.title: What this covers
lore.content: The ten-minute log after an indoor or beach match, a gym night or a tournament day, in the order that keeps the set scores, the lineup and the box score honest. It runs on top of rule/recording_a_match and rule/stats and only adds the volleyball order of operations. It owns the tags box-score, no-box-score and exhibition on volleyball events and stat lines.

lore.title: Logging a match
lore.content:
1. Find the match. search_entities entity_type event, the season tag, the date and the two sides. A scheduled event usually exists; update it rather than creating one. In a tournament, find or create the parent tournament event first and make the match PART_OF both the parent and the season.
2. Score it before anything else, in this order: the set scores as the owner says them, home (first-named) side first in every pair; count the sets to get home_score and away_score (sets won, never rally points); write score_display in the strict format "25-21, 23-25, 25-19, 25-27, 15-12" and the same sets in periods as {number, home, away} objects; result home_win or away_win (draw only in a fixed-set rec format at 1-1); decided_by only when it was not regulation (forfeit, retired, time_limit, golden_set); status completed; COMPETED_IN result on both edges. Read the sets back in one line ("3-2, 25-21 23-25 25-19 25-27 15-12, on the books"). If the owner gives a sets result without set scores, store the sets, leave periods empty and score_display as the sets result ("3-1"), and say point ratio will skip this match until the set scores come.
3. Ask one question: "Do you have the box score or the lineup?" If no: tag the event no-box-score and stop at the score and a Summary lore chunk. If yes or partly: tag box-score and take the lines.
4. Lineup, if the competition is lineups-tracked: PLAYED_IN per player with for_team, started true and lineup_order 1-6 for the starting rotation of set one, position L for the libero with started false and played true, played false for unused bench. Check six, no duplicates, no libero in the six, at most two liberos; say what you checked. Rotations by set and libero replacements go in event lore titled Rotations and Libero. Subs from outside the roster: a one-night PLAYS_FOR edge (arrangement substitute) and a Subs lore line.
5. Player match lines: one stat_line per player per match, scope match, subject_kind player, RECORDED_IN the event, STAT_OF the person, for_team when the person has two open roster edges (always for beach, where it is the pair's slug), sets_played always, the pack's keys, null for anything not kept, completeness full when every key was kept and partial when anything is null. Tag: volleyball, stats, the season tag, the player's slug fragment. Confirm first when it is more than eight new lines.
6. Team match line: sets_played, team totals, substitutions_used, timeouts_used, challenges when tracked; never sets won or set scores.
7. Roll up in the same breath: each player's season line (derived, games_played = match lines, sets_played summed, as_of the match date, Derived from chunk listing the lines) and both teams' season lines (wins/losses, the result family, table points, sets_won/lost, rally_points_for/against, forfeit counts, matches_booked).
8. The story: Summary, Key moments, Conditions (wind and sun matter on the beach) in the owner's words; a Player of the Match is a WON edge to the event.
9. Say it back in two lines: the result with the set scores and the new record or table position, and what the box score covered ("Box score for all 9; digs not kept").

lore.title: Tournament day
lore.content:
A beach event or an indoor weekend is one parent event (event_type match, stage group_stage, name "<Season> <Tournament>", date_* day one, end_date the last day) with every match PART_OF it. Before the first match: COMPETED_IN from each team or pair to the parent with side neutral_first, group ("Pool C") and seed. Log pool matches with stage group_stage and round "Pool C"; order each pool by the Standings algorithm from the pool's matches only and say who advances when the owner asks. Bracket matches take stage round_of_16 / quarterfinal / semifinal / final / consolation with round for the placing ("5th place"). At the end: final_rank on each COMPETED_IN edge to the parent, WON from the winning team or pair to the parent event with title Champion, and the season table or tour standings updated if the competition keeps one across tournaments (House rules say how tournament placings turn into tour points; store those as points on the season line and the placings in lore titled Tour results).
Beach pairs: search for the pair by both surnames before creating it; a new partner means a new pair (team_type pair), each player PLAYS_FOR it from this tournament, and the old pair goes inactive only when the owner says they have split for good.

lore.title: Quoting numbers
lore.content:
Before quoting a hitting percentage, kills per set or a leaderboard: count the team's completed matches, count those tagged box-score, and lead with the coverage: "Over the 6 matches with a box score, Jo is hitting .281 on 112 swings, 3.4 kills a set." Per-set rates divide by the player's own sets_played, never the team's. Qualifying minimum for a leaderboard: 2 attack attempts per team set played for hitting, 1 set played in half the team's matches for per-set rates, unless House rules set one; list the unqualified under a "not enough swings" line rather than hiding them. Nulls: skip, never zero; a derived rate uses only lines where every component is non-null. Blocks and points: state the convention (half an assist, or a full point per blocker) you used. Exhibition-tagged lines are never summed into season or career lines. A typed-in season figure (source owner or official) that disagrees with your sum is reported with both numbers and never overwritten.
Standings: rebuild from the edges and set scores per the Standings chunk, say how many matches had set scores on file, and name the tiebreaker that split any tied teams; for beach, pool by pool.
